output.reason_for_conversation: exploring alternatives to stopping a medication
output.summary: User with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate reported severe nausea every Saturday and Sunday after taking all six weekly tablets at once, and was considering stopping the medication despite it helping their joints. The bot explored several established strategies: adjusting folic acid timing (user was taking it on the same day as methotrexate), splitting the weekly dose, adding anti-nausea medication, and switching to injectable methotrexate. User agreed to start small changes this weekend (moving folic acid to Sunday, taking tablets with food) and to bring a prepared list to their rheumatologist appointment in two weeks. The conversation ended with the user feeling they had options and a clear plan, rather than the binary choice of suffering or quitting.
